  "confidence": 0.5,
  "anomalies": [
    {
      "category": "open_connection",
      "components": ["D23", "D28", "D45"],
      "pins": ["D23.2", "D28.2", "D45.2"],
      "nets": ["/NET0044"],
      "observed": "The anodes of the three Ethernet/status LEDs D23, D28 and D45 are all on /NET0044, and no other pin is on that net. The net is not tied to +3V3 or any driver, so the LED anodes float. Their cathodes are driven through R55, R18 and R99 from the CM4 Ethernet LED and PI_nLED_Activity outputs.",
      "expected": "LED anodes should be tied to the 3.3 V rail (as the other LED anodes in the design are, e.g. D3, D14 and D19 via +3V3 series resistors) so that the cathode-side drivers can sink current through the LEDs.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"15\") (name \"/NET0044\") (class \"Default\") (node (ref \"D23\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"A\") (pintype \"passive\")) (node (ref \"D28\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"A\") (pintype \"passive\")) (node (ref \"D45\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"A\") (pintype \"passive\")))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"103\") (name \"NET0118\") ... (node (ref \"Module2\") (pin \"95\") (pinfunction \"nPI_LED_PWR\")"}
      ],
      "impact": "The three LEDs cannot conduct from the anode side, so the Ethernet activity/link and PI activity indicators stay dark and give no status feedback.",
      "confidence": 0.45
    },
    {
      "category": "wrong_value",
      "components": ["R47"],
      "pins": ["R47.1", "R47.2"],
      "nets": ["VOUTN", "VOUTP"],
      "observed": "R47 is valued 24k, but its library description and MPN both describe a 24 Ω part (MPN FRC0805J240TSD, '24Ω 0805'). The value field and the part identity disagree by three orders of magnitude.",
      "expected": "The resistor value should match the purchased part (24 Ω if the FRC0805J240 part is intended, or the MPN and description should be corrected to a 24 kΩ part).",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(comp (ref \"R47\") (value \"24k\") ... (description \" 125mW Thick Film Resistors 150V ±100ppm/℃ ±5% 24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor - Surface Mount ROHS\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(field (name \"MPN\") \"FRC0805J240TSD\")"},
        {"source": "spice", "quote": "R47 VOUTN VOUTP 24k"}
      ],
      "impact": "If the 24 Ω part is actually fitted across the high-voltage PoE rail, it would load the supply heavily. If the value is simply mislabelled, the BOM and build are inconsistent.",
      "confidence": 0.35
    },
    {
      "category": "wrong_component_type",
      "components": ["R14", "U21", "U9"],
      "pins": ["R14.1", "R14.2", "U21.5", "U9.4"],
      "nets": ["/NET0015", "GND"],
      "observed": "/NET0015 is the output node of the open-drain SN74LVC1G07 buffer U9 (Y), and it drives the TXS0101 OE (U21.5) and the gate of Q16. The only pull resistor on this node, R14, is returned to GND rather than +3V3. An open-drain output can only pull this node low, so with R14 to GND the node can never go high, keeping U21 disabled and Q16 off.",
      "expected": "An open-drain driver node needs a pull-up to the logic rail (as R9, R84 and R46 do elsewhere) so that it can be released high.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(comp (ref \"R14\") (value \"10K\") ... (libsource (lib \"MotorController\") (part \"TAYLOR_RESISTOR\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"9\") (name \"/NET0015\") ... (node (ref \"U21\") (pin \"5\") (pinfunction \"OE\") (pintype \"input\")) (node (ref \"U9\") (pin \"4\") (pinfunction \"Y\") (pintype \"output\")))"},
        {"source": "spice", "quote": "R14 0 /NET0015 10k"}
      ],
      "impact": "The WS2812 level shifter (U21) is never enabled and the LED-ground switch Q16 is never turned on, so the status LED chain would not respond.",
      "confidence": 0.25
    }
  ],
  "summary": "The most likely anomaly is a floating LED anode net (/NET0044) that leaves three status LEDs unpowered. Lower-confidence candidates are a 24k/24Ω value mismatch on R47 and a pull-down on an open-drain node (R14). The rest of the power, CAN, USB and Ethernet wiring looks consistent with the design."
}

anomalies.observed: The anodes of the three Ethernet/status LEDs D23, D28 and D45 are all on /NET0044, and no other pin is on that net. The net is not tied to +3V3 or any driver, so the LED anodes float. Their cathodes are driven through R55, R18 and R99 from the CM4 Ethernet LED and PI_nLED_Activity outputs.
anomalies.expected: LED anodes should be tied to the 3.3 V rail (as the other LED anodes in the design are, e.g. D3, D14 and D19 via +3V3 series resistors) so that the cathode-side drivers can sink current through the LEDs.
anomalies.impact: The three LEDs cannot conduct from the anode side, so the Ethernet activity/link and PI activity indicators stay dark and give no status feedback.

anomalies.observed: R47 is valued 24k, but its library description and MPN both describe a 24 Ω part (MPN FRC0805J240TSD, '24Ω 0805'). The value field and the part identity disagree by three orders of magnitude.
anomalies.expected: The resistor value should match the purchased part (24 Ω if the FRC0805J240 part is intended, or the MPN and description should be corrected to a 24 kΩ part).

evidence.quote: (comp (ref "R47") (value "24k") ... (description " 125mW Thick Film Resistors 150V ±100ppm/℃ ±5% 24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor - Surface Mount ROHS")

anomalies.impact: If the 24 Ω part is actually fitted across the high-voltage PoE rail, it would load the supply heavily. If the value is simply mislabelled, the BOM and build are inconsistent.

anomalies.observed: /NET0015 is the output node of the open-drain SN74LVC1G07 buffer U9 (Y), and it drives the TXS0101 OE (U21.5) and the gate of Q16. The only pull resistor on this node, R14, is returned to GND rather than +3V3. An open-drain output can only pull this node low, so with R14 to GND the node can never go high, keeping U21 disabled and Q16 off.
anomalies.expected: An open-drain driver node needs a pull-up to the logic rail (as R9, R84 and R46 do elsewhere) so that it can be released high.
anomalies.impact: The WS2812 level shifter (U21) is never enabled and the LED-ground switch Q16 is never turned on, so the status LED chain would not respond.
